A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. All 28 pages of v2 and 30 pages of v3, including Appendices A–F, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results, and ablations in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The probability-based objective family, NLL and −p objectives, gradient weighting, and token-thresholding procedures are unchanged. Adaptive objectives are suggested as future work, not introduced as a method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover mathematical and medical reasoning, figfont puzzles, general instruction tuning, coding, seven low-resource languages, and clean/noisy OpenBookQA. The expanded experimental overview in v3 describes coverage already present in v2's appendices.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same base-model, NLL, −p, and thresholded-NLL comparisons and objective variants. Newly cited related work does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same sample counts, model-size sweeps, learning rates, batch sizes, training budgets, decoding settings, and metrics. The expanded discussion of experimental controls does not change the detailed protocols.

E4.justification: The token-quantile thresholding, objective-convexity, training-likelihood, model-scaling, and OpenBookQA label-noise analyses are retained with the same evidence. No new ablation or robustness test is added.

E5.justification: Run and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including averaging 16 generations per math example and reporting seed 42 for medical and figfont evaluation. The new call for better uncertainty quantification is a future direction, not a reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Matched main and appendix tables retain their numerical entries, and all six existing figures retain their graphics. v3 Figure 1 replots v2 Table 1's accuracies of 17.00, 32.75, and 31.50; its displayed differences are arithmetic restatements, not new outcomes.

T1.justification: Assumptions 6.1 and E.1 add the condition 2/V < 0.55 for the uniform model-weak predictor. The accompanying explanation explicitly separates it from the model-strong threshold. The theorem statements and proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a model-capability continuum governing the relative suitability of prior-leaning objectives and NLL, without a universally preferable fixed objective. The central empirical and theoretical contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds practical guidance, possible pretraining applications, adaptive-objective directions, and specific limitations involving stylized theory, miscalibration, and confident hallucinations. Section 4.3 also emphasizes within-domain scaling, although saying only model scale changes overstates control given Appendix C.2's differing learning rates and batch sizes.

D1.justification: The new acknowledgements disclose use of Delta and DeltaAI computing facilities. The two-H200-GPU setup, implementation details, hyperparameters, and code-access information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gao et al. (2023) to contextualize probability-based evaluation and Aghajanyan et al. (2021) to position KL regularization as prior-leaning. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for already cited works; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits streamline the abstract, expand the experimental overview, replace the short Conclusion with a longer Discussion, correct author text, and add acknowledgements. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The small motivating table becomes an accuracy plot in v3 Figure 1. Several captions are clarified, figures and tables are repositioned or renumbered, and conference headers are added. Existing plots and remaining table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and qualification through Section 7's explicit capability-proxy limitations, the vocabulary condition in Assumptions 6.1/E.1, and a more legible motivating figure. The experiments remain unchanged. Section 4.3's overstated control language is a drawback, but the clearer applicability guidance and limitations provide a limited net improvement.
